original_question: Suppose the natural numbers are finitely coloured. Determine whether there must exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n>=1} such that every finite sum a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ... + a_k y_k with each coefficient a_i in {1,2} and with a_1=a_k=1 has the same colour.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact combinatorial pattern in the paper: a finite colouring of the natural numbers, an infinite sequence (y_n), and the requirement that all sums a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ... + a_k y_k with coefficients a_i in {1,2} and endpoint constraints a_1 = a_k = 1 be the same colour.
missing_details: The universal quantifier should be made explicit: the question is for every finite colouring of the natural numbers, equivalently for every r-colouring c: N -> [r].
It should be explicit that (y_n) is a sequence of natural numbers (positive integers).
It should be explicit that the condition must hold for all lengths k >= 1.
For each k, the coefficients a_1, ..., a_k are arbitrary subject only to a_i in {1,2} for all i and a_1 = a_k = 1.
"Has the same colour" should be made stand-alone by saying that the whole set of all such sums is monochromatic.
To avoid over-strengthening the problem, it is worth stating that the paper does not add any requirement that the sequence be increasing or have distinct terms.
refined_question: For every finite colouring c: N -> [r] of the positive integers, does there exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n>=1} of positive integers such that the set {a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ... + a_k y_k : k >= 1, a_i in {1,2} for all 1 <= i <= k, and a_1 = a_k = 1} is monochromatic under c?
justification: The draft is essentially an almost verbatim restatement of the paper's Question 7.1, and the distinctive coefficient pattern a_i in {1,2} with a_1 = a_k = 1 makes the match unambiguous. The nearby paragraph explains the intended scope: this is exactly the reduced natural-number colouring problem that arose from a special colouring question on N^2, so the faithful refinement is to keep the question at that precise level and only make the quantifiers and monochromatic-set formulation fully explicit.
